requirement:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute, with an optional `SurrogateType` property, to MessagePack.Annotations. The source generator now finds partial classes that carry the attribute and implement `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`, and writes the formatter body into them. By default the formatter is contractless: public read-write members are written under their names as string keys. With a surrogate, keys and membership come from the surrogate's `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` attributes. The formatter is registered in `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019–022) cover invalid usage. The change also adds README and analyzer docs, a dependency-free ExternalTypes test project, execution tests and generator diagnostic tests.
story.why: REQ-2129 asks that Project B can source-generate a formatter for a type that lives in Project A, which cannot reference MessagePack. The requirement suggests a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute on a partial class that implements `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
touches_beyond_requirement: New public API `GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute.SurrogateType`. This surrogate design is not one of the three options the issue listed for keys and Union.
Four new user-visible analyzer rules MsgPack019–MsgPack022 plus release notes and docs.
A public record `GeneratedFormatterRequest` added to the source generator assembly.
The shared formatter T4 templates now emit `partial class` instead of `internal sealed class` when `IsUserDeclaredFormatter` is set.
GeneratorUtilities now excludes attributed classes from hand-written formatter discovery.
The MapModeExecutionTests project now excludes the new test files, so map mode is not exercised for this feature.
story.confidence_overview: High confidence that the attribute, the pipeline wiring, the template switch and the four diagnostics behave as described. The diagnostics have focused verifier tests. Low confidence in contractless mode: `CreateContractlessMembers` loops to `targets.Count - 1`, so the last member in name order (e.g. `Label`, `Y`) is never serialized. Several execution tests should therefore fail in the real run. Surrogate mode looks correct for the tested int-key case; the string-key, missing-key and duplicate-key paths are untested.

findings.description: Off-by-one: the loop runs `i < targets.Count - 1`, so contractless mode silently drops the last member in ordinal name order. Examples: ExternalPerson.Label, ExternalPoint.Y. A type with a single member serializes nothing. Data is lost on round-trip, and ContractlessClassRoundTrips, ContractlessClassUsesStringKeysForPublicReadWriteMembers, ContractlessStructRoundTrips and MessagePackObjectCanContainExternalTypes should fail.

Surrogate members are enumerated without an accessibility filter. A private or non-public field or property on the surrogate that has no [Key] or [IgnoreMember] triggers MemberNeedsKey and blocks generation.

GeneratedFormatterRequest holds INamedTypeSymbol values in the incremental pipeline. Symbols do not compare equal across compilations, which defeats incremental caching and keeps compilations alive. The collector also runs twice per formatter (model pipeline and diagnostic pipeline).

NoDeserializingConstructor is created with only a location and no message arguments. If the existing descriptor's message has placeholders, the reported message will be malformed. This path is untested.

IsPartial checks only the formatter itself. MsgPack019.md says nesting types must be partial too, but a non-partial containing type is not diagnosed and will produce a raw compiler error in generated code.

The formatted type is created with `new T()`. `required` members of T that are not serialized (excluded by the surrogate) would make the generated code fail to compile, and this case is not diagnosed.
